📚 Engine 63 — Compartment Study Guide

Engine 63 sets itself apart with 50 ft of 5" LDH on the front bumper, a gate valve and hydrant wrench mounted directly on top of the bumper, a 28-foot extension ladder, a dual foam system (Eco-Gel + Chief Eductor), a standalone HCN meter, SCBA in the cab, and the Hurst Combi Tool. Pay special attention to the ⭐ E63 Unique Items section before your first shift.

Click any card to expand. Use search to find any tool instantly.

📋 Click Here for More Details and Photos of Engine 63

🚒

Front of Engine

50 ft of 5" on bumper · Gate valve + hydrant wrench on bumper · Storz to steamer
⚠️
E63-Specific — 50 ft of 5" on the FRONT BUMPERMost engines store their short LDH section in the engineer's compartment or rear bay. Engine 63 keeps its 50 ft of 5" on the front bumper. Coming from E60/E61/E62, reset your muscle memory — don't hunt in the rear for a front section that lives up front on this rig.
FRT-01
50 Feet of 5" LDH — Front Bumper
AKA: Front LDH, finish section, five-inch, supply hose
+
📖What it is

A 50-foot section of 5" large-diameter hose stored on the front bumper — accessible without opening any compartment. First LDH section on the rig, immediately reachable.

❓Why it's needed

Front-mounted LDH is deliberate. The engineer or officer grabs this instantly for a nurse tanker hookup or short supply lay. Fast water supply starts here — before any compartment door opens.

🔧How to use
  1. Confirm hose is free and couplings are clear.
  2. For nurse tanker: connect one end to intake, route to pump panel.
  3. For short lay: connect to hydrant outlet, walk to engine.
  4. Storz coupling = quarter-turn — confirm locking lug fully seated before charging.
💡
Unique to E63 in This FleetNo other rig stores LDH on the front bumper. Direct mutual aid crews explicitly: "Front of the rig" — not "engineer's comp."
▶ Watch: LDH Forward Lay Technique
FRT-02
Gate Valve + Hydrant Wrench — Top of Bumper
AKA: Gate valve, gated valve; hydrant wrench, hydrant key
+
📖What it is

Gate valve: An inline gate-style valve (sliding internal gate, opened with a handwheel through several full turns — NOT a ball valve) controlling flow independently of the pump panel. Hydrant wrench: Operates the hydrant operating nut. Both are physically mounted on top of the front bumper — visible and accessible on arrival without searching any bag.

❓Why it's needed

Pre-staged on the bumper means the engineer grabs everything for a hydrant connection in one motion. No compartment to open, no bag to search. This is engineered for speed.

🔧How to use
  1. Gate valve: thread onto hydrant outlet before connecting hose. Leave closed. Open slowly once lines are ready — avoids water hammer.
  2. Hydrant wrench: open operating nut slowly (counterclockwise typically). Full open = when stem stops turning. Never leave partially open.
⚠️
Open Hydrants SlowlyA sudden surge creates water hammer that can blow couplings, damage the hydrant, and knock crew down. Crack the nut slowly, listen for flow, then open fully.
FRT-03
Storz-to-Steamer Adapter — Front Bumper
AKA: Storz adapter, LDH adapter, steamer adapter
+
📖What it is

Converts the Storz end of 5" LDH to connect to a hydrant's 4½" steamer port (NST threaded). Stored alongside the gate valve and hydrant wrench on the front bumper — three tools in one grab.

❓Why it's needed

Bridges Storz (quarter-turn) and NST (threaded) coupling systems, allowing 5" LDH to connect to the hydrant's highest-flow steamer outlet.

⚠️
Seat Storz FullyA half-turned Storz will blow off under pressure. The locking lug must be fully engaged. Physically verify before charging the line.
🔩

Engineer's Compartment

Top · Middle · Bottom — Fittings, hydrant bag, eductor, hose roller
Top Shelf
ENG-01
Eye Protection
AKA: Safety glasses, goggles, eye-pro
+
📖What it is

Safety glasses or goggles for eye protection during overhaul, extrication, and any debris-generating task.

❓Why it's needed

Flying debris from ceiling pulls, glass shards from extrication, chemical splashes — eyes don't get a second chance. Habit: overhaul starts, eye-pro goes on.

ENG-02
Fog Nozzle
AKA: Combination nozzle, adjustable nozzle, fog tip
+
📖What it is

Adjustable-pattern nozzle: straight stream through wide fog by rotating the bale. Engineer's spare.

🔧How to use
  1. Straight stream: base of fire, maximum reach.
  2. Narrow fog (15–30°): compartment knockdown.
  3. Wide fog (60°+): crew protection at door, exposure.
⚠️
No Fog in Confined SpacesWide fog in a smoke-filled corridor converts to steam instantly. Steam burns lungs. Straight stream for interior attack.
ENG-03
Deck Gun Nozzle
AKA: Master stream tip, monitor tip, deck gun tip
+
📖What it is

Removable nozzle for E63's deck gun, stored in engineer's compartment when not in use.

❓Why it's needed

Stored safely when not mounted. A damaged or missing tip = no master stream.

⚠️
Lock Before FlowingVerify the tip is fully locked onto the monitor before charging. A tip that blows off at master stream pressure becomes a dangerous projectile.
ENG-04
Double-Ended Spanners
AKA: Spanner wrench, coupling wrench
+
📖What it is

Bar wrenches with different-sized jaws on each end for tightening or breaking loose hose couplings.

❓Why it's needed

Couplings tighten under pressure — hand-uncoupling after flowing is impossible. Spanners provide leverage without damaging threads.

✅
Bleed Before SpannerringAlways bleed residual pressure from the line before uncoupling. Even low pressure resists uncoupling and sprays when coupling breaks free.
ENG-05
Gated Wye
AKA: Wye, gated wye, Y-connector, Wye valves, Wye ball valves
+
📖What it is

Y-fitting with one 2½" inlet and two independently-gated 1½" outlets.

🔧How to use
  1. Connect inlet to supply.
  2. Connect attack lines to each outlet.
  3. Open outlets independently as crews are ready.
  4. One line can be shut while the other flows — critical for standpipe ops.
❓Why it's needed

Splits one supply into two independent attack lines. Two crews work simultaneously off one standpipe port.

ENG-06
Adaptors — M2M, F2F, CFD, Reducer
AKA: Double male, double female, CFD coupler, sexless adapter
+
📖What's here

M2M: connects two female ends. F2F: connects two male ends. CFD: Chicago Fire Department thread for mutual aid. Reducer: steps down diameter.

❓Why they're needed

Mismatched couplings happen in the field. These bridge all gaps. CFD couplings = mutual aid interoperability.

💡
Mutual AidKnow where your CFD adapters are before a mutual aid assignment. Finding them under pressure on a Chicago fire scene is not acceptable.
Middle Shelf
ENG-07
Storz to Steamer (Middle Shelf)
AKA: Storz adapter, spare adapter
+
📖What it is

Second Storz-to-steamer adapter on the middle shelf — backup to the front bumper unit.

❓Why it's needed

Two adapters allow simultaneous connections at two points: one at the hydrant, one for a second supply or tanker hookup.

ENG-08
Storz to 1½"
AKA: Storz reducer, LDH to small-line adapter
+
📖What it is

Reduces a Storz LDH coupling to a 1½" NST connection, allowing small-diameter lines to be fed from large-diameter supply couplings.

❓Why it's needed

Allows 1½" attack lines to be fed directly from LDH supply or large apparatus outlets.

ENG-09
30-Degree Elbow Storz — Anti-Kink
AKA: Angled Storz, elbow Storz, offset Storz
+
📖What it is

Storz coupling with a 30-degree offset angle for LDH connections where a straight coupling would create a kink at the pump intake or a tight hydrant port.

❓Why it's needed

A kinked 5" line at a sharp angle can lose hundreds of GPM. The elbow provides a smooth directional change — maximizing water delivery.

💡
Reach for This on Tight ConnectionsAt an awkward hydrant or cramped pump panel: elbow Storz first. A smooth connection flowing 1,500 GPM beats a straight one kinked to 800.
ENG-10
Hydrant Bag — Full Contents
AKA: Hydrant kit, hydrant pack
+
🔧Contents
  • Gate valve
  • Hydrant wrench
  • Pipe wrench
  • Rope + hook (to move charged 5" hose)
  • 2 small spanners
  • 2 double-ended spanners
  • Storz-to-steam connectors
  • Storz reducer (to 1½")
  • CFD coupler
  • Rubber mallet
📖What it is

Single bag with everything needed for a hydrant connection. One grab = complete hydrant toolkit.

❓Why it's needed

Speed and completeness. The hydrant person takes this bag and has every tool. What you leave behind is what you'll need.

✅
Grab the Whole BagDon't cherry-pick. Every second at the hydrant is a second the engine runs on tank water.
💡
Rope + Hook for Charged 5"A charged 5" line weighs hundreds of pounds per section. The rope and hook in this bag let 1–2 people reposition it — otherwise it takes 5.
Bottom Shelf
ENG-11
Chief Eductor 125 GPM (Fill Tube in Middle Container)
AKA: Foam eductor, in-line eductor, proportioner, POK eductor
+
📖What it is

A 125 GPM in-line foam eductor (POK/Chief brand). Venturi draws concentrate through the pickup/fill tube. Critical: fill tube is in the middle container — NOT in the eductor bag itself.

🔧How to use
  1. Get fill tube from middle container first.
  2. Connect eductor inline between pump discharge and attack line.
  3. Insert fill tube into concentrate.
  4. Set eductor percentage to match concentrate (1%, 3%, 6%).
  5. Maintain min. 100 GPM — below this venturi collapses.
  6. Keep tube submerged — air = plain water.
❓Why it's needed

Foam/gel dramatically improves Class A suppression and Class B vapor control. The eductor is what makes it possible without a separate foam proportioning system.

⚠️
FILL TUBE IS IN THE MIDDLE CONTAINEROn most rigs the pickup tube is with the eductor. On E63 it is in the MIDDLE CONTAINER. If you can't find the tube, your foam system is dead. This is the #1 unique fact about E63's foam setup.
⚠️
Minimum Flow CriticalBelow ~100 GPM the venturi stops working and you're flowing plain water while thinking you're applying foam. Maintain adequate pressure.
▶ Watch: Foam Eductor Operation
ENG-12
Hose Roller
AKA: LDH dewatering roller, hose squeeze roller, water/air-removal roller
+
📖What it is

Used to remove air and water from a large diameter hose after a working incident — when the line is uncharged and being broken down for repacking. The hose is fed through the roller, which squeezes out residual water and trapped air so the hose can be loaded clean and dry.

❓Why it's needed

5" LDH holds an enormous amount of residual water — a single 100-foot section can have gallons trapped inside after the pump is shut down. That water adds weight, makes the hose harder to repack neatly, and can freeze the load in winter. The roller squeezes out air and water in one pass so the hose loads back the way it should.

🔧How to use
  1. After pump shutdown, disconnect the hose ends.
  2. Position the roller at one end and feed the hose through it.
  3. Walk the hose through the roller — the squeeze pushes water and air out the trailing end.
  4. Reload the hose into the bay or onto the rack as it comes out the back of the roller — clean and dry.
💡
Unique to E63Know where it lives and how to use it before you're at the back of the rig with 1,000 feet of soaked LDH and a wet engine bay.
ENG-13
5" Hose — 25 ft (Bottom Shelf)
AKA: Short LDH, finish section, nurse tanker section
+
📖What it is

A 25-foot 5" LDH section in the bottom shelf — a second short supply section. E63 total short LDH: 50 ft (front bumper) + 25 ft (here) + 50 ft (officer first compartment) = 125 ft.

❓Why it's needed

Two sections can be in use simultaneously: front section at hydrant, this one at a tanker. The third provides extension. E63 is set up for flexible, multi-source water supply.

🪓

Middle Compartment — Driver's Side

Irons · Maul · K-tool · Officer's tool
MDD-01
Fire Axe / Pickhead Axe
AKA: Pick axe, pickhead axe, fire axe
+
📖What it is

Axe with cutting blade on one side, pointed pick on the other. For roof ventilation, floor breaching, wall opening.

🔧How to use
  1. Roof vent: pick pierces decking, blade cuts rafters/sheathing.
  2. Floor breach: pick breaks surface, blade widens hole.
  3. Driving Halligan: use flat of blade as striking face — never the pick.
MDD-02
Flat Head Axe
AKA: Flat axe, striking axe, fire axe
+
📖What it is

Axe with flat striking face and cutting blade. Drives the Halligan and cuts structural members.

❓Why it's needed

The other half of "the irons." Flat face drives Halligan with precision and force.

✅
Irons Travel TogetherFlat axe + Halligan = the irons. If you have one, partner has the other. Never separated on scene.
MDD-03
Sledgehammer / Maul
AKA: Sledge, mall, striking tool
+
📖What it is

Heavy sledgehammer for commercial steel doors, high-security padlocks, and masonry — more mass than the flat axe.

🔧How to use
  1. Two-person: one holds Halligan, one drives with sledge.
  2. Communicate: "Set?" → "Ready!" → swing.
  3. For padlocks: strike the shackle, not the lock body.
MDD-04
Halligan Bar
AKA: Hooligan, Pro-bar, the bar, Halligan tool
+
📖What it is

30" forged steel forcible entry tool — adze/fork on one end, pick + flat adze on the other. The most versatile forcible entry tool in the fire service.

🔧How to use
  1. Place adze into door gap near lock.
  2. Drive in with flat axe face.
  3. Rotate to gap frame.
  4. Push fork behind bolt and lever open.
❓Why it's needed

Opens doors, pulls ceilings, breaches floors, vents roofs. The Swiss Army knife of fireground tools.

⚠️
Try Before You PryTry the door handle first — more doors are unlocked than you expect.
▶ Watch: Halligan Door Forcing
MDD-05
K-Tool (Added After Photos)
AKA: Lock puller, K-tool, cylinder puller
+
📖What it is

"K"-shaped tool that extracts lock cylinders from commercial doors without destroying the door — allows key tool operation of exposed mechanism.

🔧How to use
  1. Slide over lock cylinder.
  2. Drive down with axe to bite cylinder.
  3. Lever cylinder out with Halligan.
  4. Use key tool on exposed mechanism.
⚠️
Added After Photos — Confirm LocationK-tool was added AFTER compartment was photographed. It IS on the rig — verify its exact location on your first rig check.
▶ Watch: K-Tool Technique
MDD-06
Officer's Tool / Pry Axe (Added After Photos)
AKA: Captain's tool, officer's tool, pak-tool, pro-tool
+
📖What it is

Compact multi-purpose pry/strike tool sized for an officer to carry with a radio — prying edge, striking face, and hook in a lightweight form.

❓Why it's needed

Officers need a tool they can carry without dropping communications. Enough capability to force a door or pry debris solo.

💡
Also Added After PhotosBoth K-tool and officer's tool were added post-photography. Physically verify both on your first check.
🧯

Rear Compartment — Driver's Side

Second Halligan · Axes · Extinguishers · Step ladder
💡
Sledgehammer + Pick Axe Added After PhotosThe source document notes these were added after the compartment was photographed. They ARE present — photos do not reflect current configuration. Verify on first shift.
RDD-01
Halligan (Rear — Second Set)
AKA: Hooligan, bar, Pro-bar
+
📖What it is

Second Halligan in the rear driver's compartment. Provides forcible entry capability from the rear of the apparatus.

❓Why it's needed

Two Halligans = two crews can force different entry points simultaneously. Front crew uses middle compartment irons; rear crew uses rear irons.

RDD-02
Flat Head Axe (Rear)
AKA: Flat axe, striking axe
+
📖What it is

Second flat axe stored in the rear driver's compartment, partnering the rear Halligan for a complete second set of irons.

❓Why it's needed

Rear-accessible irons — the crew at the back of the rig doesn't have to go around to the middle compartment.

RDD-03
Sledgehammer + Pickhead Axe (Rear — Added Post-Photos)
AKA: Sledge, maul; pick axe — added after photos
+
📖What they are

Sledgehammer and pickhead axe added to the rear driver's compartment after the compartment documentation was photographed. Both are present — photos do not show them.

❓Why they're needed

Redundancy. Rear crew has heavy striking and breaching capability without reaching the middle compartment.

⚠️
Not in Photos — But They're ThereDocument explicitly states these were added after the pic. Physically verify position on your rig check.
RDD-04
Silver Bullet — Pressurized Water Extinguisher
AKA: Water can, silver bullet, stored-pressure water
+
📖What it is

Stainless steel pressurized water extinguisher (~2.5 gallons) for Class A fires — ordinary combustibles.

🔧How to use
  1. Remove from mount.
  2. Remove safety pin.
  3. Aim at base of fire.
  4. Squeeze handle.
  5. Sweep side to side at fire base.
❓Why it's needed

Fast Class A knockdown without pulling a hose line. Precision cooling during overhaul.

⚠️
Class A ONLYNever on energized electrical (electrocution) or hot cooking oil (violent steam explosion). Know your fire class first.
RDD-05
Pump Can
AKA: Pump can, garden sprayer, Indian pump
+
📖What it is

Hand-operated pump sprayer delivering controlled low-pressure water stream — precision tool for small fires and overhaul hot-spot cooling.

❓Why it's needed

Sometimes you need a cup of water in exactly the right spot, not 125 GPM. Precision overhaul tool, pairs with TIC.

RDD-06
ABC Dry Chemical Extinguisher
AKA: Dry chem, multi-purpose extinguisher, monoammonium phosphate
+
📖What it is

Multi-purpose dry chemical extinguisher for Class A, B, and C fires. Monoammonium phosphate powder.

🔧How to use (PASS)
  • Pull the pin
  • Aim at base of fire
  • Squeeze the handle
  • Sweep side to side
💡
Residue WarningABC dry chem is corrosive and ruins electronics. Use CO₂ on sensitive equipment when possible.
RDD-07
Small Step Ladder
AKA: Step ladder, A-frame, folding step
+
📖What it is

Compact self-supporting folding ladder for short elevation access — vehicle rooflines, elevated controls, precision elevated work.

❓Why it's needed

Faster than a ground ladder for short access problems. Self-supporting — no leaning point needed.

🏗️

First Compartment — Officer's Side

Akron coping tool · High rise bag · 50 ft of 5"
PAS-01
Akron Brass Hose Hoist — Coping Tool
AKA: Coping tool, hose hoist, hose pulley, standpipe hose guide
+
📖What it is

Akron Brass brand cast metal hose management tool that hooks over railings, window sills, or balcony edges to redirect and support hose being hauled up through stairwells. The tool takes the abrasion load instead of the hose jacket.

❓Why it's needed

Hauling hose up concrete stairwells destroys the hose jacket through abrasion. The coping tool redirects the hose over a smooth surface — protecting it and allowing a small crew to hoist significant lengths.

🔧How to use
  1. Hook over railing or sill at target floor.
  2. Feed hose through or over coping tool before hauling.
  3. Station crew member at tool to guide hose.
  4. Below feeds, above pulls — tool bears friction load.
💡
Also on E60Akron hose hoist is on E63 and E60. Not on all engines. If you haven't seen this tool before, review it before you're at floor 15 with hose to haul.
▶ Watch: Standpipe Hose High-Rise Ops
PAS-02
High Rise Bag — Contents
AKA: Standpipe bag, hi-rise kit
+
🔧What's in it
  • 6-foot length of 1¾" hose
  • 90-degree coupling
  • Pressure gauge
  • Vise grips (for stiff standpipe valves)
  • Spanner wrench
📖What it is

Immediate-deploy standpipe bag for high-rise floor operations. Smaller and faster to grab than the High Rise Pack.

❓Why it's needed

High-rise standpipe: connect to building system at the floor below the fire. This bag has every fitting, pressure monitor, and connection tool in one grab.

⚠️
Two Floors Below — AlwaysNEVER take the elevator to the fire floor. Two floors BELOW, then stairs. An elevator opening on the fire floor traps you in smoke and heat.
💡
Pressure Gauge Is CriticalStandpipe pressures vary wildly. Always monitor with the T-connector gauge (target ~100 psi residual) before opening the nozzle.
▶ Watch: Standpipe Operations
PAS-03
50 Feet of 5" — Officer Side
AKA: Short LDH, finish section
+
📖What it is

Third 50-foot 5" LDH section. E63 short LDH total: 50 ft (front bumper) + 25 ft (engineer's bottom shelf) + 50 ft (here) = 125 ft of short supply hose.

❓Why it's needed

Two sections can run simultaneously — hydrant and tanker. Third provides extension. E63 is a strong supply engine.

🔐

Middle Compartment — Officer's Side

High rise pack · Bolt cutters
PMD-01
High Rise Pack
AKA: Standpipe pack, hi-rise pack, skid load pack, shoulder load pack
+
📖What it is

The High Rise Pack refers to a skid load — packed for carrying on the shoulder — that contains 150' of 1¾" hose. It's the attack-line component of E63's standpipe operation: shoulder it, walk it up the stairwell, drop it on the staging floor, and connect into the standpipe outlet using the fittings from the High Rise Bag. Larger complement to the High Rise Bag in the first officer compartment.

❓Why it's needed

While the Bag handles fittings and pressure monitoring, the Pack provides the attack hose. The skid-load configuration means one firefighter can shoulder 150' of 1¾" up multiple flights without the load tangling. Together, Bag + Pack = complete standpipe operations capability.

💡
Bag AND Pack — Know the DifferenceE63 carries BOTH. The Bag (first officer comp.) = fittings + gauge. The Pack (here) = 150' of 1¾" hose, packed as a shoulder skid load. Know which is which and where each lives.
PMD-02
Bolt Cutters
AKA: Bolt cutters, chain cutters, lock cutters
+
📖What it is

Heavy-duty bolt cutters for severing padlocks, chains, hasps, and cable locks.

🔧How to use
  1. Open handles fully.
  2. Position jaws on padlock shackle — not the lock body.
  3. Smooth controlled squeeze — no jerking.
  4. For chains: position at a link, not a welded joint.
❓Why it's needed

Defeat gates, fences, padlocked doors, and chain-link fencing quickly without power tools.

⚠️
Case-Hardened Locks Resist Bolt CuttersHigh-security padlocks (Medeco, Mul-T-Lock) have hardened steel shackles. For these, use angle grinder or K-tool. Forcing a hardened shackle can permanently damage the cutter jaws.
🗄️

Rear Compartment — Officer's Side

Tool box · Cones · Tarps · Blanket · Fan hanger
PRD-01
Tool Box
AKA: Maintenance kit, hand tools, utility box
+
📖What it is

Portable hand tool box for field maintenance and utility tasks. Typical contents: screwdrivers, wrenches, pliers, socket set, tape measure, voltage tester, zip ties.

❓Why it's needed

Tools break and fittings loosen in the field. Self-sufficient engineering capability without returning to the station.

⚠️
Voltage Tester — Use It Every TimeIf there's a voltage tester in this box, use it before touching any electrical component on a call. Every conductor is live until confirmed dead.
PRD-02
Traffic Cones
AKA: Road cones, pylons, safety cones
+
📖What it is

High-visibility orange traffic cones for scene perimeters and roadway incident safety.

❓Why it's needed

Vehicle strikes kill firefighters. Cones go out before you open any compartment at a roadway incident.

⚠️
Cones First, Compartments SecondAt roadway incidents: scene safety first. Cones out before you grab anything else. The temptation to rush to the patient is real. A struck firefighter makes two patients.
PRD-03
Tarps
AKA: Salvage covers, tarps, poly sheeting
+
📖What it is

Waterproof tarps for salvage — protecting building contents from water damage during and after firefighting.

❓Why it's needed

Salvage prevents secondary water damage that often exceeds fire damage in value. Deploying tarps during attack protects what the fire didn't reach.

PRD-04
Blanket
AKA: Emergency blanket, patient blanket, thermal blanket
+
📖What it is

Emergency thermal blanket for patient warming and protection from debris during rescue operations.

❓Why it's needed

Hypothermia is a serious complication in trauma and cardiac patients. Warm the ground AND the patient — not just the top.

PRD-05
Fan Hanger
AKA: PPV bracket, fan mount, window fan frame
+
📖What it is

Bracket suspending a PPV fan in a doorway or window — hands-free ventilation without a crew member holding the fan.

🔧How to use
  1. Secure hanger in door/window frame.
  2. Mount fan — adjust to cover full opening.
  3. Start fan only after fire is controlled/suppressed.
❓Why it's needed

Hands-free PPV frees one firefighter for attack, rescue, or overhaul. One bracket = one more productive crew member.

⚠️
Never PPV an Active FirePushing air into an active fire feeds oxygen and can cause flashover. Coordinate with attack crew before starting.
🚗

Rear of Engine

Middle · Right side · Left side · Hose bays
Middle Rear Compartment
REAR-01
Decon Bucket — Dawn Soap + Brush
AKA: Decontamination bucket, decon kit, post-fire decon
+
📖What it is

Bucket with Dawn dish soap and scrub brush for post-incident tool and equipment decontamination.

🔧Decon Protocol
  1. Scene: Fire Wipes (cab) on exposed skin before entering apparatus.
  2. Rig: Fill bucket, scrub tools, gloves, and boots before stowing.
  3. Station: Bag gear, shower before eating or touching face.
  4. Never: Contaminated gear home or in personal vehicle.
❓Why it's needed

Fireground carcinogens (PAHs, benzene, heavy metals) deposit on every surface. Decon at the scene prevents cab and station contamination.

⚠️
Decon Is Cancer Prevention EquipmentFirefighter cancer rates are elevated from carcinogen exposure. This bucket is not optional. Use it after every working fire. 90 seconds that could save your life.
REAR-02
Garden Hose
AKA: Wash-down hose, utility hose, decon hose
+
📖What it is

Garden hose for low-pressure utility use — rinsing tools with the decon bucket, flushing contaminants, gentle overhaul wetting.

❓Why it's needed

The decon bucket without water is just a bucket. Garden hose provides the rinse. Also useful for cooling hot spots during overhaul without committing an attack line.

REAR-03
Hurst Combi Tool — Cuts AND Spreads
AKA: Combi tool, combination tool, jaws of life (combo)
+
📖What it is

E63-specific. The Hurst Combi Tool is a single hydraulic tool whose blades both CUT (like a cutter) AND SPREAD (like a spreader). E63 and E60 use a Combi. E61/E62 carry separate Cutter + Spreader.

❓Why it's different

Lighter, faster to set up — one tool instead of two. Trade-off: with separate tools, two crew members work simultaneously. With Combi, one operation at a time. Sequence matters.

🔧How to use
  1. Connect to power source.
  2. For spread: position open blades at gap, activate.
  3. For cut: position perpendicular to target, activate close.
  4. Never cut at angle — perpendicular gives clean cuts.
  5. Keep 6" minimum from airbag/SRS components.
⚠️
Plan Your SequenceIf trained on E61's separate tools, reset for E63. ONE tool does both. Plan ahead: spread the door THEN cut hinges. Simultaneous operations are impossible.
⚠️
EV/Hybrid — Identify FirstEVs carry 300–800V battery packs. Cutting wrong areas without disabling 12V aux can electrocute crew. Check ERG before starting extrication.
▶ Watch: Hurst Combi Tool Extrication
REAR-04
2 Shovels — Scoop and Pointed
AKA: Scoop shovel, spade, mop-up shovel
+
📖What they are

Scoop: flat blade for debris, absorbent, loose material. Spade: pointed for digging and compacted material.

❓Why they're needed

Overhaul, hazmat cleanup, absorbent application. Right tool for loose material AND ground-penetrating work.

Right Side Rear — New York Hooks
REAR-05
6 ft Pike, 8 ft NY Hook, 10 ft NY Hook (Right Side)
AKA: Pike pole, NY hook, New York hook, plaster hook, drywall hook
+
📖What they are

6 ft Pike: Standard hook/pick for ceiling and wall pulls. 8 ft + 10 ft New York Hooks: Narrower purpose-designed hooks — narrow profile fits between studs better than standard pike. Right side: 6 ft pike, 8 ft NY Hook, 10 ft NY Hook.

🔧How to use
  1. Pull TOWARD you and to the side — NEVER directly overhead.
  2. Work from a doorway or corner.
  3. 6 ft: tight hallways. 10 ft: standoff distance and tall spaces.
❓Why they're needed

Overhaul requires pulling burned material to expose hidden fire. NY hooks are superior for modern drywall — narrow tip fits between studs cleanly.

✅
Pull Toward You — Never Over YouCeiling material is extremely heavy when wet. Work from a doorway and pull toward you. Never stand under what you're pulling.
Left Side Rear — Pike Poles
REAR-06
6 ft, 8 ft, 10 ft Pike Poles (Left Side)
AKA: Pike pole, ceiling hook, overhaul hook
+
📖What they are

Three pike poles in increasing lengths on the left side rear: 6 ft, 8 ft, 10 ft. Standard hook-and-pick tips.

❓Why three lengths

6 ft: tight attics and small rooms. 8 ft: standard ceiling height. 10 ft: tall commercial spaces or maximum standoff from dangerous overhead material.

Rear Hose Bays
🚒Rear Hose Bay Summary
LocationLoadNozzle/TypeNotes
Top — Left1,000 ft — 5"StaticLong relay supply; Storz couplings
Top — Middle150 ft 2½" skid + 400 ft 3"Smooth bore on skidSkid deploys off 3" supply bed
Top — Right150 ft 1¾" skid + 500 ft 3"Breakaway fog (75 psi, 150 gpm)Attack line off 3" supply

REAR-07
Crosslays — 200 ft 1¾" ×2 (Top and Bottom)
AKA: Crosslay, minuteman, pre-connect
+
📖What it is

Two 200-foot 1¾" preconnected crosslays — a top crosslay and a bottom crosslay in the middle hose bed. Both accessible from either side. Both preconnected.

❓Why it's needed

Two stacked crosslays = two distinct attack lines simultaneously deployable from either side. Primary residential attack hose.

✅
Know Top vs. BottomWith stacked crosslays, pulling the wrong line or both creates a tangle. Know which crosslay is yours before the call.
REAR-08
Skid Loads — 2½" and 1¾"
AKA: Skid load, minuteman load, attack pack
+
📖2½" Skid

150 ft 2½" with smooth bore nozzle, loaded on 400 ft 3" supply hose. Pull skid; 3" deploys behind it.

📖1¾" Skid

150 ft 1¾" with breakaway fog nozzle (75 psi, 150 gpm) on 500 ft 3" supply hose.

⚠️
Breakaway Nozzle — Check ItBreakaway mechanism must be functional or the skid won't free from the supply bed cleanly. Check on every rig check.
🧪

Middle Compartments — Eco-Gel / Foam System

95 gpm nozzle · 95 gpm eductor · Eco-Gel · Pickup tubes · Oil Dry
💡
E63 Has a Dedicated Eco-Gel System — Different From E60's Chief Eductor FoamE63 has a complete Eco-Gel system: 95 GPM nozzle, 95 GPM eductor, 5× 5-gallon Eco-Gel buckets, foam aeration tube, and pickup tubes. This is a DIFFERENT system from the Chief Eductor 125 GPM in the engineer's bottom shelf. Operational instructions are posted in the compartment. Read them before your first shift.
FOAM-01
95 GPM Nozzle
AKA: Eco-Gel nozzle, foam nozzle, low-flow nozzle
+
📖What it is

Nozzle specifically calibrated for 95 GPM — matched to E63's 95 GPM eductor system. Must be used together as a matched pair.

❓Why it's needed

Foam eductors are flow-sensitive. Mismatched nozzle breaks venturi effect and stops foam induction. The 95 GPM nozzle IS the correct match for E63's 95 GPM eductor.

⚠️
Match Nozzle to Eductor — AlwaysNever substitute a different flow-rate nozzle. A 125 GPM nozzle on a 95 GPM eductor destroys venturi effect — you'll be flowing plain water thinking you're applying gel.
FOAM-02
95 GPM Eductor
AKA: Foam eductor, venturi proportioner
+
📖What it is

95 GPM in-line eductor using venturi effect to draw Eco-Gel from buckets through pickup tube and mix into water stream at correct ratio.

🔧How to use
  1. Insert pickup tube into Eco-Gel bucket.
  2. Connect eductor inline between pump discharge and 95 GPM nozzle.
  3. Set percentage per Eco-Gel specs (see posted instructions).
  4. Maintain 95 GPM — below this venturi collapses.
  5. Keep pickup tube submerged — surface air = plain water.
❓Why it's needed

Eco-Gel adheres to surfaces and penetrates deep-seat fires far better than plain water. The eductor converts plain water to Eco-Gel solution.

💡
Posted InstructionsEco-Gel operational instructions are posted IN the compartment. Read and review them on every rig check.
FOAM-03
5-Gallon Eco-Gel Buckets — ×5
AKA: Eco-Gel concentrate, Class A foam, fire gel
+
📖What it is

Five 5-gallon containers of Eco-Gel fire suppression concentrate — 25 gallons total. Dramatically increases water's penetrating ability and heat absorption while adhering to surfaces.

❓Why it's needed

Class A foam/gel pretreats exposures, suppresses deep-seat fires faster with less water, and clings to surfaces where plain water runs off immediately.

🔧How to use
  1. Place bucket where pickup tube reaches.
  2. Keep tube at bottom of bucket throughout.
  3. Switch to next bucket when one empties — without stopping.
  4. Never mix Eco-Gel with other concentrate types.
✅
Check All 5 Buckets on Rig CheckA partially-used bucket that wasn't refilled is a gap in foam capacity. Check each one.
FOAM-04
Foam Aeration Tube
AKA: Aeration tube, aspirating attachment, air-aspirating tube
+
📖What it is

Introduces air into the foam solution stream to create fully-expanded foam. Without it, you're applying wetting agent. With it, you're applying true expanded foam that clings to vertical surfaces and floats on burning liquids.

❓Why it's needed

Fully aerated foam has dramatically different properties: clings to vertical surfaces, floats on burning fuel, provides sustained vapor suppression. The tube is what makes true foam vs. just wet solution.

💡
Aeration = True FoamWithout the aeration tube, Eco-Gel solution flows as liquid — useful but not maximum effectiveness. With the tube, it becomes true expanded foam that stays where you put it.
FOAM-05
Eductor with Pickup Tube (Second System)
AKA: Secondary eductor, pickup tube set
+
📖What it is

A second eductor and pickup tube assembly in the middle compartment. E63 has TWO foam systems: the 95 GPM Eco-Gel system (here) AND the 125 GPM Chief Eductor (engineer's bottom shelf).

❓Why two systems

Different concentrates and flow rates for different scenarios. 95 GPM Eco-Gel: Class A suppression and exposure protection. 125 GPM Chief Eductor: higher-flow operations.

⚠️
Chief Eductor Pickup Tube Is Stored HereThe pickup tube for the engineer's Chief Eductor is stored in the middle compartment — NOT in the engineer's compartment with the eductor. Know this. If you're deploying the Chief Eductor, its tube is here.
FOAM-06
Foam Nozzle — 75 psi, 125 GPM
AKA: Foam nozzle, aspirating nozzle
+
📖What it is

A dedicated foam nozzle rated at 75 psi operating pressure and 125 GPM — matched to higher-flow foam operations. Separate from the 95 GPM nozzle matched to the Eco-Gel eductor.

❓Why it's needed

The correct nozzle for the Chief Eductor 125 GPM system. Match nozzle to eductor flow rate for proper venturi operation.

FOAM-07
Oil Dry / Kitty Litter
AKA: Absorbent, granular absorbent, clay absorbent
+
📖What it is

Granular clay absorbent for soaking up fuel, oil, and liquid hazards. Stored in a separate container from the Eco-Gel system within the middle compartment area.

❓Why it's needed

Fuel spills = fire and slip hazards. Environmental regulations require containment. Absorbent neutralizes the hazard and prevents storm drain contamination.

💡
Separate ContainerOil Dry is in "other middle officer side container" — separate from Eco-Gel system components. Confirm exact position on rig check.
🪜

Top of Engine — Ladders

28' Extension · 16' Roof · 10' Folding
💡
E63 Has a 28-Foot Extension Ladder — Longer Than Most EnginesMost Glen Ellyn engines carry a 24-foot extension. Engine 63 carries a 28-foot, giving additional reach for third-floor windows that other engines can't ladder from the same position. Know this — it changes your size-up options on arrival.
LAD-01
28' Extension Ladder
AKA: Ground ladder, extension ladder, 28-footer
+
📖What it is

28-foot two-section aluminum extension ladder — longer than the 24-footers on E60/E61/E62. Reaches third-floor windows and elevated access points other engines cannot cover from the same position.

🔧How to use
  1. 1-to-4 rule: 1 ft out per 4 ft height (28 ft extended = ~7 ft base from building).
  2. Tip extends 3 rungs above roofline or window sill.
  3. Spotter foots the ladder until secured.
  4. Heel against building before climbing.
❓Why it's needed

Rescue from upper floors. Firefighter access and egress. The extra 4 feet vs. a 24-footer is the difference between reaching a third-floor sill or not.

⚠️
Throw Early — Before You Need ItLadders belong up on arrival, before conditions require a rescue. A ladder thrown after a Mayday is almost always too late.
▶ Watch: Ground Ladder Placement
LAD-02
16' Roof Ladder
AKA: Roof ladder, hook ladder, single-section ladder
+
📖What it is

16-foot single-section ladder with folding roof hooks at the top. Hooks deploy over a roof ridge to anchor the ladder on steep-pitch roofs — turns the ladder into a stable walkway.

🔧How to use
  1. Carry to roof on the extension ladder.
  2. At ridge: deploy hooks by swinging open and hooking over peak.
  3. Lean back against roof slope — hooks hold it in place.
  4. Walk and work on the rungs.
❓Why it's needed

Roof ventilation on pitched roofs requires stable footing. Without roof hooks, anything over 4:12 pitch is dangerously unstable.

⚠️
Sound the Roof Before Committing WeightBefore stepping onto a fire-weakened roof, sound with your hook or axe — hollow sound = compromised decking. Throw the ladder but don't commit weight until you know the surface.
LAD-03
10' Folding Ladder
AKA: Attic ladder, folding ladder, interior ladder
+
📖What it is

Compact 10-foot folding ladder for attic access through standard 22"×30" ceiling hatches, sub-floor access, and short elevation gains in confined areas.

❓Why it's needed

Attic fires require above-ceiling access. Only ladder that fits through standard attic openings. Also for mechanical room platforms and short-elevation interior challenges.

⚠️
Test Attic Floors Before EnteringSound the attic floor with a hook before sending a firefighter up. Fire rapidly weakens lightweight truss construction. The ladder gets you to the opening — judgment determines if it's safe to enter.
🚨

Cab Compartment

AED · 4-Gas · Gas Trac · HCN meter · SCBA pack · Knox Box
Medical
CAB-01
AED — Automated External Defibrillator
AKA: AED, defib, defibrillator, shock box
+
📖What it is

Analyzes cardiac rhythm and delivers calibrated electrical shock to restore normal rhythm in VF/VT cardiac arrest.

🔧How to use
  1. Power on — follow audio/visual prompts.
  2. Attach pads per pad labels.
  3. Clear: "I'm clear, you're clear, everybody's clear!"
  4. AED analyzes — do NOT touch patient.
  5. Shock when prompted.
  6. Resume CPR immediately after shock.
❓Why it's needed

Cardiac arrest survival drops ~10% per minute without defibrillation. AEDs make early shock possible without ALS.

⚠️
Clear Before ShockingEVERYONE must be clear. Contact during defibrillation delivers current to the bystander. Announce then shock.
▶ Watch: AED Operation
Gas Detection — Three Meters on E63
💡
E63 Carries THREE Gas Meters — Including a Standalone HCN MeterE63 has: 4-gas monitor, Gas Trac (methane/HCN combo), AND a dedicated standalone HCN meter. This is more gas detection capability than most rigs. Know all three — what each detects and when to use each.
CAB-02
4-Gas Monitor
AKA: Multi-gas monitor, 4-gas meter, Gas Track Monitor
+
🔧What it detects
GasAlarmIDLH
CO35 ppm1,200 ppm
O₂<19.5% / >23.5%<16%
H₂S10 ppm50 ppm
Combustible (%LEL)10% LELvaries
❓Why it's needed

CO, H₂S, and combustible gases are invisible at lethal concentrations. O₂ deficiency incapacitates in seconds. The 4-gas meter detects what your senses cannot.

⚠️
Bump-Test Before Every ShiftA monitor with failed sensors reads safe when it isn't. Bump-test to verify alarm response. Never trust an untested meter.
CAB-03
Gas Trac — Methane / HCN
AKA: Gas tracker, methane meter, HCN meter
+
📖What it is

Monitors methane (natural gas) and hydrogen cyanide (HCN) — combination unit.

❓Why it's needed

Methane creates explosive atmospheres before ignition. HCN — produced by burning plastics and synthetics — is 35× more toxic than CO by concentration.

⚠️
HCN Is Dangerously UnderestimatedVictims appearing to be smoke-inhalation cardiac arrests may be HCN-poisoned. Standard CPR alone will not reverse HCN toxicity. Report exposure to EMS immediately for antidote consideration.
CAB-04
HCN Meter — Standalone
AKA: Hydrogen cyanide detector, cyanide meter, dedicated HCN sensor
+
📖What it is

Dedicated standalone hydrogen cyanide detection meter — a SECOND HCN sensor separate from the Gas Trac. E63 has dual HCN detection: integrated in Gas Trac AND this standalone meter.

❓Why it's needed

Redundancy and cross-check capability. Two sensors can be deployed to different areas of a large incident. Readings can be confirmed between units.

💡
E63-Specific Dual HCNMost rigs have HCN only through Gas Trac. E63 has both. Use the standalone for confirmation or second-location monitoring.
CAB-05
SCBA Pack — In Cab
AKA: Air pack, SCBA, airpack, self-contained breathing apparatus
+
📖What it is

Complete SCBA unit stored in the cab — cylinder, regulator, harness, and face piece immediately accessible from the cab door.

❓Why it's needed

Cab-mounted SCBA means any crew member can don air before dismounting if conditions warrant. Also serves as backup to compartment SCBAs.

⚠️
Low Air = Exit NowWhen the low-air alarm sounds, exit immediately — not when the task is done. One-third supply remaining. Declare Mayday if disoriented.
▶ Watch: SCBA Donning
CAB-06
Knox Box Key
AKA: Knox key, rapid entry key, master key
+
📖What it is

Secured master key opening Knox Box rapid-entry systems on commercial buildings — immediate access without forced entry.

❓Why it's needed

After-hours commercial calls. Opens the box in seconds, building key inside opens the structure cleanly.

⚠️
Secure at All TimesThis key opens hundreds of buildings. Loss requires re-keying the entire Knox system. Never leave it unsecured.
CAB-07
Water Bottle
AKA: Crew water, hydration supply
+
📖What it is

Water in the cab for crew hydration.

❓Why it's needed

Firefighting causes extreme exertion and heat stress. Dehydration impairs performance before you feel thirsty. Drink proactively.

💡
Hydrate Before, Not Just AfterFluid loss starts the moment you don gear. Drink before the call if possible, immediately after coming out of a working fire.
☀️

Top of Engine

Empty water bottle · Foam/Gel · Manifold
TOP-01
Empty Water Bottle — Foam Operations Container
AKA: Foam fill bottle, concentrate vessel
+
📖What it is

A large empty container on top of the engine — intentionally empty. Used as a dedicated transfer vessel for Eco-Gel operations. NOT a drinking water container.

❓Why it's needed

Foam operations sometimes require transferring concentrate to a smaller working vessel. The dedicated empty bottle keeps chemical transfer separate from potable water containers.

⚠️
This Is NOT For DrinkingThe top-of-engine empty bottle is a foam operations vessel. Crew water is in the cab. Never cross-contaminate.
TOP-02
Foam/Gel Supply — Top of Engine
AKA: Eco-Gel, foam concentrate, Class A foam
+
📖What it is

Additional Eco-Gel concentrate or foam supply stored on top of the engine — supplementing the 5-gallon buckets in the middle compartment.

❓Why it's needed

Extended foam operations deplete the middle compartment supply quickly. Top-of-rig supply allows resupply without interrupting operations.

TOP-03
Manifold
AKA: Foam gun manifold, deck gun manifold, water manifold
+
📖What it is

Multi-inlet/outlet distribution fitting combining multiple supply line inputs into a single outlet for high-volume master stream or foam gun operations.

❓Why it's needed

The deck gun needs more volume than a single discharge outlet efficiently provides. The manifold combines multiple supply lines into the gun for maximum flow. In foam ops, routes solution from eductor into deck gun.

✅

Front Dash — Communications

Gray mic = DuCom · Black lower-left = Fireground · Black upper-right = PA
DASH-01
DuCom — Gray Microphone
AKA: DuCom, dispatch radio, county radio, main radio
+
📖What it is

The gray push-to-talk microphone connected to the DuPage County interoperable radio system (DuCom). This is the primary channel for dispatch — assignments, address updates, resource requests, and scene status reports all go through here.

❓Why it's needed

Dispatch is your lifeline. Every call-related communication that doesn't involve fireground tactical coordination runs through DuCom. Losing contact with dispatch is a serious safety gap.

🔧How to use
  1. Confirm correct county/district channel before the call.
  2. Press and HOLD the PTT (push-to-talk) button.
  3. Wait 1 full second — the repeater needs time to key up.
  4. "Utility 62 to DuCom…" then your message.
  5. Release PTT, wait for acknowledgment.
  6. Never talk over another unit — listen before transmitting.
⚠️
1-Second Pause Before SpeakingKey the mic and immediately talking clips your first words. "Utility 62" becomes "tility 62." Pause one second after pressing PTT — then speak.
💡
Gray = Dispatch, Black Lower-Left = FiregroundThree mics, three different systems. Mixing them up on scene causes significant problems. Know which is which before you roll.
DASH-02
Fireground Microphone — Black, Lower Left
AKA: Tac mic, fireground channel, tactical radio
+
📖What it is

The black PTT microphone at the lower-left of the dash, connected to the tactical (fireground) radio channel. Used for crew-to-crew and unit-to-command communication at a working incident.

🔧How to use
  1. Confirm the correct tac channel for this incident.
  2. PTT → wait 1 second → speak: "Utility 62 at [location], [message]."
  3. Keep transmissions short and specific.
  4. Critical traffic: prefix with "Emergency Traffic" before your message.
❓Why it's needed

Separates scene communications from dispatch traffic. Command and crews coordinate on tac; county dispatch stays on DuCom.

⚠️
Mayday — Do Not HesitateMAYDAY, MAYDAY, MAYDAY — [name] — [unit] — [location] — [problem]. Loud and clear. Immediately. Do not downplay a developing emergency to avoid "bothering" command.
DASH-03
PA System Microphone — Black, Upper Right
AKA: PA, public address, exterior speaker, loudspeaker
+
📖What it is

The black microphone at the upper right, connected to the external public address speaker. Broadcasts your voice outside the vehicle without opening a window.

❓Why it's needed

Roadway incident control, bystander management, and directing traffic without leaving the cab. Your voice carries over engine and ambient noise at full PA volume.

💡
Use PA for Traffic ControlAt MVAs, directing approaching drivers and pedestrians through the PA keeps your crew focused on the incident instead of doing manual traffic control. Efficient use of a built-in tool.
🗂️

Glove Compartment

Maps · ERG · Flares · Passport · Loading guide
GLV-01
District Maps
AKA: Street atlas, paper nav, A-to-Z maps
+
📖What it is

Physical paper street maps of the response district. The no-battery, no-signal backup navigation system that works when the MDT freezes, GPS drops, or a crew member's phone is dead.

🔧How to use
  1. Pre-fold to your district before you need it.
  2. Orient to direction of travel.
  3. Cross-reference nearest intersection to confirm routing.
  4. Know major arteries and hydrant corridors so the map confirms — not discovers.
⚠️
Technology Will FailMDTs crash, GPS drops, cell service disappears in remote areas and underground. The crew that reads a paper map still arrives on time. The crew that can't is guessing.
GLV-02
Truck Loading Instruction Paper
AKA: Load chart, weight distribution guide
+
📖What it is

A reference sheet describing proper equipment loading for Utility 62 — weight distribution, tie-down requirements, and placement to maintain safe vehicle handling.

❓Why it's needed

Equipment thrown back in haste after a call gets placed wherever it fits. Improper weight distribution affects braking and handling — the loading guide ensures the rig handles safely on every response.

GLV-03
Patient Prepare Reports — Blank
AKA: PCR, patient care reports, run reports, medical forms
+
📖What it is

Blank paper patient care reporting forms for documenting medical incidents. Demographics, chief complaint, vitals with timestamps, interventions, and crew information.

🔧How to use
  1. Record: name, DOB, address, chief complaint.
  2. Vitals with timestamps — initial and trending.
  3. Interventions applied and when.
  4. Crew names and ID numbers.
  5. Write legibly — this is a legal and medical record.
⚠️
Legibility Is a Legal StandardIllegible PCRs create liability and can result in disciplinary action. Take the 30 seconds to write clearly every time.
GLV-04
Vehicle Name Laminate — "Utility 62"
AKA: Rig ID tag, unit identifier, apparatus card
+
📖What it is

A laminated card identifying this apparatus as "Utility 62." Used in the Passport accountability system and for visual apparatus identification at multi-unit incidents with mutual aid.

❓Why it's needed

At busy multi-unit incidents, correct apparatus identification prevents command confusion. This laminate also anchors the Passport system to this specific unit.

GLV-05
Spare Tire Lock Key — In Bag
AKA: Spare tire key, anti-theft key, lug lock key
+
📖What it is

A specialized key required to unlock the anti-theft lug nut securing the spare tire mount. Without it, the spare cannot be removed — even with a jack and full lug wrench set.

❓Why it's needed

A flat tire on a loaded utility vehicle is an out-of-service event. This key is the single point of access to the spare. Know exactly where it is before you have a nighttime flat on a busy road.

⚠️
Find This Key Before You Need ItHunting for the spare key at the side of a road at 2 AM with equipment to transport is a miserable and avoidable situation. It's in a bag in the glove compartment. Locate it on your first rig check.
GLV-06
Road Flares — ×2
AKA: Highway flares, fusees, emergency road flares
+
📖What it is

Two pyrotechnic road flares, burning 15–30 minutes and visible over a mile away in daylight, much further at night. Used to alert approaching traffic of a hazard zone ahead.

🔧How to use
  1. Remove the cap.
  2. Strike the friction cap against the striking surface — firm stroke.
  3. Hold away from body at first ignition — intense initial flare.
  4. Place in the road BEFORE the scene (100, 200, 300 ft back) on a 50 mph road.
  5. NEVER near fuel spills or leaking vehicles.
⚠️
Flares + Fuel = IgnitionAt any MVA with fuel leakage, fuel smell, or liquid on the road — DO NOT light flares. Use LED or reflective devices only. A burning flare at a fuel spill can ignite vapors instantly.
💡
Place Them Far BackDrivers at 50 mph cover 100 feet in less than 1.5 seconds. A flare at 100 feet gives almost no reaction time. Place them 300+ feet back on any arterial road.
GLV-07
Passport Accountability System
AKA: Passport, accountability boards, velcro tags, name tags
+
📖What it is

A physical firefighter accountability system using velcro name tags on a Passport board. The driver collects tags from crew members and places them upside down on the board. The white velcro Passport goes to the Incident Commander. The red velcro Passport stays with Utility 62. Command uses this to know exactly which personnel are assigned to this unit at all times.

🔧How to use
  1. Collect name tags from all crew boarding Utility 62.
  2. Place tags upside-down on the Passport board.
  3. White Passport → hand to IC or Accountability Officer on arrival.
  4. Red Passport → stays with Utility 62 at all times.
  5. Update immediately when crew members reassign or leave scene.
⚠️
Upside-Down Is the System — Not a MistakeTags go on upside-down by design. It takes a deliberate action to read them, reducing accidental removal. In a Mayday, the IC reads your tag and knows your assignment instantly.
✅
No Tag = Not AccountableIf your name tag isn't on the Passport, Command doesn't know you're on scene. In a rapid intervention situation, that delay can be life-altering.
▶ Watch: Passport Accountability System
GLV-08
Emergency Response Guidebook — ERG
AKA: ERG, orange book, hazmat book, DOT guidebook
+
📖What it is

The U.S. DOT Emergency Response Guidebook — initial hazmat response reference. Yellow pages: 4-digit UN/NA numbers in numerical order → guide number in Orange section. Blue pages: material names alphabetically → guide number. Orange pages: response guides — health hazards, fire/explosion risk, PPE, evacuation procedures, first aid, spill control. Green pages: initial isolation/evacuation distances for toxic inhalation hazards. Over 50 gal = large spill. Distances vary by spill size and day vs. night. Back pages: emergency phone numbers including CHEMTREC (1-800-424-9300).

🔧How to use
  1. Identify material — read placard number or name.
  2. Yellow pages: look up 4-digit UN/NA number → find guide number.
  3. Blue pages: look up by name if no number visible.
  4. Orange pages: go to that guide number for hazards, PPE, initial actions.
  5. Green highlighting in yellow/blue → also check Green pages for evacuation distances.
  6. Green pages: find spill size (small/large), time of day → isolation distance.
⚠️
Green = Toxic Inhalation or Water ReactiveGreen-highlighted materials in the yellow/blue pages are either toxic inhalation hazards or produce toxic gas on contact with water. These have evacuation zones in the Green pages — check them immediately.
💡
UN vs. NA NumbersBoth are 4-digit codes. UN numbers are international; NA numbers are North America-specific. Both work identically in the ERG — look them up the same way.
▶ Watch: How to Use the Emergency Response Guidebook
🦺

Door Pockets — Driver + Officer

Roadway vests × 2
DOOR-01
Roadway Safety Vests — ×2 (One Per Door)
AKA: Hi-vis vest, ANSI vest, traffic vest, reflective vest
+
📖What it is

ANSI Class II or III high-visibility retroreflective safety vests stored in the driver's and officer door pockets. Neon yellow-green or orange with silver reflective tape — mandatory PPE at any roadway incident.

❓Why it's needed

NFPA 1500 and OSHA require high-visibility PPE at roadway incidents. Turnout gear retroreflective tape is NOT a substitute — it's designed for fire conditions, not traffic visibility. A separate hi-vis vest is required.

🔧How to use
  1. Don BEFORE stepping out at any roadway incident.
  2. Put it on inside the cab — not after stepping into traffic.
  3. Zip or snap all closures — a flapping vest doesn't protect.
  4. Wear OVER turnout coat if gear is on.
  5. Inspect retroreflective tape — damaged tape doesn't reflect at night.
⚠️
On Before Your Feet Hit the GroundThe most dangerous moment at a roadway incident is stepping out of the apparatus. Vest goes on INSIDE the vehicle before the door opens. Two seconds — every single time.
💺

Front Bench + Back Seat

PPE (sterile gloves & masks) · 4 Radios
SEAT-01
PPE — Sterile Gloves & Masks
AKA: Body Substance Isolation (BSI), medical PPE, exam gloves, surgical/N95 masks
+
📖What it is

The PPE on Utility 62 refers to sterile gloves and masks only — not bunker gear / not turnouts. Stocked in the front bench and back seat are nitrile exam gloves (multiple sizes) and disposable face masks (a mix of surgical and N95-style respirators) so crew can don Body Substance Isolation (BSI) PPE for medical contacts, blood/body-fluid scenes, suspected infectious patients, and decon support.

🔧How to use
  1. Don gloves BEFORE patient contact — never after.
  2. Pick a size that fits — too tight tears, too loose lets fluids in at the cuff.
  3. For respiratory infection contact, add a surgical mask; for known airborne hazards, use an N95 (mold the nose-piece for a seal).
  4. Doff gloves inside-out without skin contact, drop in red biohazard bag.
  5. Wash hands at the first opportunity — gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene.
❓Why it's needed

Utility 62 is a support / medical-response apparatus, not an interior fire-attack rig. The PPE it carries matches its mission: BSI for patient care, basic respiratory protection for sick patients and overhaul-adjacent work. Structural firefighting PPE (coat, pants, helmet, hood, SCBA) is on the engines and is donned from your locker — not from this rig.

⚠️
This Rig Does NOT Carry Bunker GearDon't go looking for turnout coats, pants, or structural helmets on Utility 62 — they're not here. If you arrive on scene and structural PPE is needed, it has to come from your locker or another apparatus. Plan accordingly.
✅
Gloves Are the Minimum, Not the TotalFor unstable patients or unknown body fluids, gloves alone aren't enough — add eye protection and a mask. Multiple sizes of each are stocked here for that reason.
SEAT-02
Portable Radios — ×4
AKA: Portables, handie-talkies, HTs, walkie-talkies
+
📖What it is

Four portable two-way radios in the back seat — one per crew member. Provides individual radio capability independent of the apparatus, allowing each crew member to communicate, receive incident updates, and transmit emergencies regardless of position on scene.

🔧How to use
  1. Check battery level every shift — minimum two bars.
  2. Confirm correct channel assignment for incident type.
  3. Secure to chest strap or radio strap — never loose.
  4. PTT → wait 1 second → unit ID → message.
  5. Keep away from immersion and extreme heat.
❓Why it's needed

Individual radios mean each crew member can hear a Mayday, receive reassignment, or transmit an emergency even if separated from the apparatus and other crew members.

⚠️
Dead Battery = No VoiceCheck every shift. A radio at 30% starting charge won't survive a multi-hour incident. A silent radio in an emergency is as dangerous as no radio.
📦

Truck Bed — Cases and Bins

MSA/SCBA · Milk crate · Water rescue bin · Throw bag · Rope · Extinguisher · Sked
BED-01
MSA Case — SCBA + Air Bottle + Face Piece (Size M)
AKA: MSA case, breathing apparatus, SCBA kit
+
📖What it is

An MSA hard case containing a complete SCBA: cylinder (air bottle), SCBA harness/regulator assembly, and a size Medium face piece. Provides respiratory protection in IDLH (Immediately Dangerous to Life or Health) environments: smoke, toxic gas, oxygen-deficient atmospheres.

🔧How to use
  1. Don harness — shoulder straps, cinch waist belt snug.
  2. Connect cylinder, open valve slowly counterclockwise.
  3. Don face piece — pull straps bottom-to-top for even seal.
  4. One inhalation to seat regulator — confirm airflow.
  5. Arm the PASS device.
  6. Confirm cylinder pressure before entry — 4,500 psi = full.
❓Why it's needed

Utility 62 may respond to hazmat incidents, confined space operations, or structural fires where respiratory protection is required. This SCBA gives the crew immediate entry capability.

⚠️
Size M Only — A Poor Seal Is Not ProtectionThis face piece is size M. An incorrect size creates gaps where contaminated air enters regardless of cylinder pressure. Know your fit size and verify before any entry.
▶ Watch: SCBA Donning and Doffing
BED-02
Milk Crate — Jumper Cables, Chocks, Tape, Hitch
AKA: Utility crate, supply bin
+
🔧Contents
  • Jumper cables — heavy gauge, 20–25 ft, for vehicle jump-starts at incidents
  • Wheel chocks — rubber or plastic wedges to prevent vehicle rolling
  • Caution tape — yellow perimeter tape for scene control
  • Receiver and hitch ball — tow hardware for trailer or light recovery operations
🔧Jumper Cables — How to Use
  1. Red (+) → dead battery (+).
  2. Red (+) → good battery (+).
  3. Black (−) → good battery (−).
  4. Black (−) → engine block or unpainted chassis on the dead vehicle — NOT the dead battery negative terminal.
  5. Run good vehicle 2 minutes, then start the dead vehicle.
  6. Remove in exact reverse order.
⚠️
Negative to Chassis — Not Dead BatteryThe dead battery vents hydrogen gas. A spark at the negative terminal can ignite it. Connect the final black cable to a metal chassis point away from the battery.
✅
Wheel Chocks Before Working Near Any VehicleAt any extrication or vehicle incident, place chocks before any crew member approaches the vehicle. A vehicle in gear can roll from vibration or secondary impact. Chocks are non-negotiable.
BED-03
Gray Bin — Water Rescue Equipment
AKA: Water rescue bin, swift water kit, rescue bin
+
🔧Contents
  • 4 Waders — chest waders for shallow water / bank operations
  • 14" inner tube — throw-assist flotation device
  • 100 lb Lift Bag — pressurized airbag, recovery of submerged items up to 100 lbs
  • 250 lb Lift Bag — recovery of heavier submerged items up to 250 lbs
  • PFD — personal flotation device for rescuer water operations
🔧Lift Bags — How to Use
  1. Position bag under, around, or against the object to be lifted.
  2. Connect air supply (SCBA low-pressure or dedicated inflator).
  3. Inflate SLOWLY — watch for sudden shift or roll of the object.
  4. Always rig a safety line — a burst bag drops the load instantly.
  5. 100 lb: smaller submerged equipment, debris.
  6. 250 lb: larger items, partial vehicle recovery support.
⚠️
Lift Bags Are for Objects — Not PeopleUsing a lift bag attached to a person creates catastrophic injury risk from sudden uncontrolled lift. These bags recover objects only.
⚠️
Waders in Moving Water = TrappedWaders that fill with water in moving current become a deadly anchor. In water above knee depth or with significant flow, waders are NOT appropriate PPE. Trained swift water rescue requires dry suit, PFD, and safety line.
▶ Watch: Underwater Lift Bag Use
BED-04
Orange Square Bag — Blanket
AKA: Rescue blanket, patient blanket, thermal blanket
+
📖What it is

An emergency thermal blanket in an orange bag for patient warming and protection from debris and environmental exposure during rescue and medical operations.

❓Why it's needed

Hypothermia is a serious complication in trauma, cardiac arrest, and drowning patients. Body temperature loss accelerates physiological deterioration rapidly. Always warm under AND over the patient — not just on top.

BED-05
Black Bag — Flood Light, Stand, Battery
AKA: Scene light kit, flood light bag, portable lighting
+
🔧Contents
  • Flood light — high-output cordless scene illumination
  • Flood light stand (yellow) — telescoping or folding mount for optimal positioning
  • DeWalt battery — cordless power supply for the light
🔧Setup
  1. Extend/unfold the stand to working height.
  2. Mount flood head to stand — confirm secure.
  3. Insert DeWalt battery into the light.
  4. Position behind apparatus when possible — light pointed at the work zone, not toward approaching traffic.
  5. Aim to illuminate crew, not headlight approaching drivers.
⚠️
Don't Light the Road — Light the Work ZoneA flood aimed toward approaching traffic creates blinding glare that makes drivers less able to see the scene, not more. Position lights so the light source is behind the work area relative to traffic direction.
BED-06
Orange/Red Bag — PFD + Throw Bag
AKA: Water rescue bag, throw bag kit, life ring bag
+
🔧Contents
  • 1 PFD (Personal Flotation Device) — USCG-approved life jacket
  • Throw bag — 50–75 ft of floating rope in a throwable bag for reach rescue
🔧Throw Bag — How to Use
  1. Open the bag top, grasp some rope in your non-throwing hand.
  2. Throw underhand, aimed past and slightly upstream of the victim.
  3. When victim grabs rope, hold firm — let current pendulum them to shore.
  4. Do NOT pull them directly toward you — let the current do the work.
  5. Repack by stuffing loosely — never coil — so rope pays out freely on the next throw.
  6. A repacked bag can be thrown again in seconds. A coiled rope tangles.
⚠️
Reach → Throw → Row → GoAttempt rescue in this order. Untrained in-water entry creates a second victim. Reach with a pole first, throw, then row, then enter the water as an absolute last resort with proper PPE and safety line.
▶ Watch: Throw Bag Water Rescue Technique
BED-07
Rope Spool — 200 ft
AKA: Utility rope, safety line, polypropylene rope
+
📖What it is

200 feet of utility rope on a spool for water rescue safety lines, perimeter control, scene management, equipment tethering, and general utility operations.

❓Why it's needed

Rope is one of the most operationally versatile tools carried on a utility vehicle. 200 feet provides significant reach for water rescue safety systems and large-area perimeter control.

✅
Utility Rope Is Not Life-Safety RopeDo not use utility rope for technical rescue, rappelling, or SCBA bailout systems. Life-safety rope is rated and certified for those uses. Know the difference before putting weight on any rope.
BED-08
ABC Fire Extinguisher
AKA: Dry chem, multi-purpose extinguisher, fire can
+
📖What it is

ABC dry chemical extinguisher effective on Class A (combustibles), Class B (flammable liquids), and Class C (electrical) fires.

🔧How to use — PASS
  • Pull the pin
  • Aim at the BASE of the fire — not the flames
  • Squeeze the handle
  • Sweep side to side
💡
Vehicle Fires — Early InterventionA small engine compartment fire is within range of this extinguisher. Open the hood slightly, insert the nozzle into the gap, sweep at the base of flames. Once the fire is established and growing — back off, establish perimeter, protect exposures.
BED-09
Sked — Foldable Rescue Stretcher
AKA: Sked, sked-evac, flexible litter, drag sled, plastic stretcher
+
📖What it is

A SKED-EVAC foldable plastic stretcher that rolls for storage and deploys flat for patient packaging and transport. The reinforced plastic shell slides across rough surfaces, fits through narrow openings, and allows hauling up stairwells with rope rigged through the head grommets.

🔧How to use
  1. Unroll and lay flat.
  2. Position patient on Sked, center them.
  3. Secure chest, waist, and leg straps.
  4. Drag using head-end handles for straight-line movement.
  5. Thread rope through head grommets for stairwell hauling.
  6. Two-person side carries for very short lifts over obstacles.
❓Why it's needed

The Sked moves patients through environments no wheeled stretcher can navigate — collapsed structures, confined spaces, steep terrain, and long drags across rough ground.

▶ Watch: Sked Stretcher Patient Packaging
🪓

Truck Bed — Tools

2 Pike poles · Halligan · Flat head axe · Umbrella · Snow scraper
TOOL-01
2 Pike Poles
AKA: Pike pole, ceiling hook, plaster hook, overhaul hook
+
📖What it is

Two aluminum-handled pike poles with hook-and-spike tips. Used for overhaul (pulling ceilings and walls), debris management, and water rescue reach assists.

🔧How to use
  1. Overhaul: position yourself at a doorway or corner.
  2. Pull wall and ceiling material toward you and to the side — NEVER overhead.
  3. Water rescue: extend toward victim from the bank.
  4. Lie down to lower your center of gravity when reaching over water.
✅
Pull Toward You — Never Directly OverheadFire-weakened, water-soaked ceiling material can weigh hundreds of pounds. It drops fast when it lets go. Work from a protected position and pull toward you.
TOOL-02
Halligan Bar
AKA: Hooligan, Pro-bar, the bar, halligan tool
+
📖What it is

30" forged steel forcible entry tool — adze and fork at one end, pick and flat adze at the other. The most versatile forcible entry tool in the fire service: doors, padlocks, ceilings, floors, overhaul.

🔧How to use
  1. Inward-swinging door: adze into gap at lock, drive with flat axe, lever to gap frame, push fork behind bolt and lever open.
  2. Outward-swinging door: fork behind door stop, lever.
  3. Padlock: hook curved adze around shackle, lever.
  4. Pulling ceiling: use the pick end to punch through and pull.
⚠️
Try Before You PryCheck the door handle first. An unlocked door that gets forced wastes time, damages property, and is embarrassing. Thirty seconds of trying before forcing saves everyone.
TOOL-03
Flat Head Axe
AKA: Flat axe, striking axe, fire axe
+
📖What it is

Fire axe with a flat striking face and cutting blade. Primary pairing with the Halligan bar — together they are "the irons," the core forcible entry combination in the fire service.

❓Why it's needed

The flat face drives the Halligan with precision force. The blade cuts structural members, roofing, and wall materials.

✅
Irons Travel TogetherHalligan + flat axe = the irons. If you pick up one, partner picks up the other. These two tools are never separated at a working incident.
TOOL-04
Umbrella
AKA: Rain cover, personal umbrella, crew umbrella
+
📖What it is

A standard umbrella for crew use during extended outdoor operations in precipitation — protecting documentation, patient care activities, and equipment from rain and snow.

❓Why it's needed

Utility 62 supports extended operations. Keeping documentation legible, electronic equipment functional, and patients protected from precipitation is a genuine operational need on long-duration outdoor incidents.

TOOL-05
Snow Scraper
AKA: Ice scraper, windshield scraper
+
📖What it is

Automotive snow and ice scraper for clearing windows before winter operations.

❓Why it's needed

Clear ALL windows before moving — front, rear, and sides. Driving with obscured windows is a crash risk and a legal violation.

⚠️
Clear All Windows — Not Just the Driver's ViewSnow covering the rear window eliminates reverse visibility. Snow on the hood slides forward when braking. Clear the entire vehicle, not just what you can see through the front glass.
🔋

Supplies — Batteries & Hydration

Spare DeWalt batteries · Water bottles
SUP-01
Spare DeWalt Batteries
AKA: Spare batteries, tool batteries, backup power
+
📖What it is

Spare DeWalt 20V MAX battery packs for the flood light and any other DeWalt cordless tools on Utility 62.

❓Why it's needed

A dead battery on the flood light mid-operation is a serious problem. Spare batteries eliminate this single point of failure and keep scene lighting continuous through extended incidents.

✅
Check Charge Every ShiftBatteries self-discharge sitting on the rig. Check and fully charge any battery below 50% every shift. A battery that was full last Friday may be at 40% today.
SUP-02
Water Bottles
AKA: Crew water, hydration supply
+
📖What it is

Water for crew hydration during and after operations.

❓Why it's needed

Physical exertion combined with PPE heat load creates rapid fluid loss. Cognitive function and physical performance decline before thirst registers. Drink proactively on every shift and after every working assignment.

💡
Hydrate Before, Not Just AfterDrink at the start of shift, before calls when possible, and immediately after coming off a working assignment. Don't wait to be thirsty.
✅
